definitions.explanation: A place where a dead person is buried; a burial site with a marker or monument.

examples.japanese: お{盆|ぼん}に{墓|はか}を{参|まい}った。
examples.english: I visited the grave during Obon.
examples.notes: 墓を参る = to visit a grave (墓参り)

examples.japanese: {先祖|せんぞ}の{墓|はか}は{京都|きょうと}にある。
examples.english: My ancestors' graves are in Kyoto.

examples.japanese: {墓|はか}に{花|はな}を{供|そな}えた。
examples.english: I offered flowers at the grave.

examples.japanese: {家族|かぞく}みんなで{墓|はか}の{掃除|そうじ}をした。
examples.english: The whole family cleaned the grave together.

examples.japanese: {祖父|そふ}が{亡|な}くなってから、{毎年|まいとし}お{彼岸|ひがん}に{墓|はか}{参|まい}りに{行|い}っている。
examples.english: Since my grandfather passed away, I visit his grave every year during the equinox.
examples.notes: お{彼岸|ひがん} = equinox period (traditional time for grave visits)

notes:
USAGE: {墓|はか} refers to individual graves or tombs. In Japan, families often share a single grave marker ({墓石|はかいし}/{墓石|ぼせき}).

COMMON PATTERNS:
・{墓|はか}{参|まい}り (visiting a grave)
・{墓|はか}を{建|た}てる (to erect a gravestone)
・{墓|はか}に{入|はい}る (to be buried)
・{墓|はか}を{掃除|そうじ}する (to clean the grave)

COMMON COMPOUNDS:
・{墓|はか}{参|まい}り (grave visit)
・{墓地|ぼち} (cemetery, graveyard)
・{墓石|はかいし}/{墓石|ぼせき} (gravestone, tombstone)
・{墓場|はかば} (graveyard)
・お{墓|はか} (grave - polite)

CULTURAL NOTE: Visiting family graves ({墓参|はかまい}り) is an important tradition in Japan, especially during お{盆|ぼん} (Obon) and お{彼岸|ひがん} (equinox periods).
